text:
maria: Quick async check — I'm about to update the public embeddings doc and want to lock the contract for empty/null handling, truncation, and batch limits before the SDK bump. Example scenarios: input = ["", null, "short", very long text]. What do we promise clients?

kevin: Quick answer: output preserves input positions. empty string -> we compute an embedding for "" (not a zero vector). null -> preserved as null in the response (no embedding object). We truncate on a per-item basis to the per-item token limit; we do NOT apply a shared batch token budget.

maria: Clarify shape: so response.data.length == input.length and positions align? If nulls are preserved, do we still return an object with embedding=null or omit the object? Need exact example for docs.

kevin: Yes — positions align 1:1. For each input element we return either {embedding: [...], index: i} or {embedding: null, index: i} for null entries. Example: ```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "input": ["", null, "hello"] }

200 OK
{
  "model": "embedder-v1",
  "data": [
    { "index": 0, "embedding": [0.001, -0.12, ...] },
    { "index": 1, "embedding": null },
    { "index": 2, "embedding": [0.02, 0.14, ...] }
  ],
  "usage": { "input_tokens": "..." }
}
```

sasha: What's the batch-size limit again? And behavior when clients exceed it — do we split server-side or return an error?

kevin: Default max_items per request = 512 for hosted API. If >512 we reject with 413 Payload Too Large and a structured error that includes "max_batch_items": 512 and "suggested_split": true. We do not silently split the request on behalf of the client because ordering/partial-failure semantics would be ambiguous. Dedicated/Private plans may have different limits surfaced via account metadata.

lee: Note for Console/SDK: we should surface the per-account limit from the control plane and provide an auto-split helper that the SDK can opt into. But server still returns 413 by default.

maria: Good call. What about items that exceed per-item token limit? Do we truncate or reject? Historically we truncated but there was chatter about a strict option.

kevin: Default behavior remains truncation (we truncate to the per-item token limit, current hosted cap = 8192 tokens per item). We added an opt-in query param/body flag named "strict_truncation" (false by default). If strict_truncation=true the API returns 422 with a clear error per-index for items that exceed token limit. This is non-breaking because default remains truncate. We'll add explicit docs and examples.

jason: Backwards-compat note: no breaking changes to v1 behavior — empty strings still embed, nulls preserved, per-item truncation default. New flags (strict_truncation) are opt-in and appear in v2+ docs only.

maria: Perfect. I'll update the doc to include the JSON example, the 413 behavior, and the strict_truncation flag. Opening a tiny PR and tagging @kevin and @sasha for review.

kevin: Sounds good, please add a small note about dedicated/private overrides. :+1:

deploy-bot: [deployed] embeddings-service config: max_items=512, per_item_token_limit=8192 (hosted) — changeset id: d7f3b2

maria: Thanks all — will ping when PR is up. :raised_hands:
